questions.q: To describe the position of an object, what must we fix first?
o: The time interval of the motion
The total length of the path
questions.a: A reference point: the position is the distance and direction of the object from this fixed point at an instant.

questions.q: On a straight market road, a bus stop is the reference point and positions to its right are positive. A handcart stands at -25 m and is then pushed 40 m to the right. What is its new position?
questions.a: +15 m: starting 25 m to the left of the bus stop and moving 40 m right takes it past the stop to 15 m on its right (-25 + 40 = +15).

questions.q: Assertion (A): A water tank whose distance and direction from the school gate stay the same all day is at rest with respect to the gate. Reason (R): An object is at rest if its position with respect to the reference point does not change with time.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A: the tank's position from the gate does not change with time, which is exactly what being at rest means.

questions.q: True or False: 'To describe the position of an object, it is enough to give its distance from the reference point.' Give the verdict and the reason.
questions.a: False. Position needs both the distance and the direction of the object from the reference point; on a straight line the direction is shown by a plus or minus sign.
s: Reason: the direction from the reference point is also needed, not only the distance

questions.q: (a) What is the difference between an instant of time and a time interval? (b) The school bell rings at 9:00 am and again at 9:40 am. Which of these is an instant and what is the time interval between them?
questions.a: (a) An instant of time is a single reading of a clock; a time interval is the duration between two instants, that is, between two clock readings. (b) 9:00 am (and 9:40 am) is an instant; the time interval between them is 40 minutes.
s: (a) Instant = one clock reading; interval = duration between two readings
(b) 9:00 am is an instant; interval = 40 minutes

questions.q: A heron walks along the straight bank of a canal. Its positions are noted from a small bridge, taking east as positive: -8 m at 0 s, -8 m at 5 s and +4 m at 12 s. (i) On which side of the bridge, and how far, is the heron at 0 s? (ii) Is it at rest or in motion between 0 s and 5 s? Give a reason. (iii) Did it cross the bridge between 5 s and 12 s? Justify.
questions.a: (i) 8 m to the west of the bridge (the minus sign means west). (ii) At rest: its position from the bridge stays -8 m, so it does not change with time. (iii) Yes: its position changes from -8 m (west of the bridge) to +4 m (east of the bridge), so it must have passed the bridge.
s: (ii) At rest: position stays -8 m, unchanged with time
(iii) Yes: sign changes from minus (west) to plus (east)

questions.q: Riya sits in a bus moving along a straight road. Read the statements. I. Riya is at rest with respect to the bus driver. II. Riya is in motion with respect to a tree on the roadside. III. Whether Riya is at rest or in motion does not depend on the reference point chosen. Which of these are correct?
questions.a: I and II only. Riya's position from the driver does not change, but her position from the tree does, so whether she is at rest or in motion depends on the reference point; statement III is wrong.

questions.q: A straight road runs east-west past a school gate S and a bus stop B, which is 200 m east of S. A water tank T is 120 m east of S. Asha takes S as her reference point with east as positive; Ravi takes B as his reference point with west as positive. (a) What position does Asha give for the tank? (b) What position does Ravi give for the tank? (c) A cyclist is at -50 m in Asha's description. What is the cyclist's position in Ravi's description? (d) Asha and Ravi give different numbers for the tank. Explain whether one of them must be wrong.
questions.a: (a) +120 m (120 m east of S). (b) The tank is 200 - 120 = 80 m west of B, and west is positive for Ravi, so +80 m. (c) -50 m for Asha means 50 m west of S, which is 200 + 50 = 250 m west of B, so Ravi writes +250 m. (d) Neither is wrong: a position is the distance and direction from the chosen reference point, so different reference points and positive directions give different numbers for the same place.
s: (b) Ravi: 80 m west of B, so +80 m
(c) Cyclist 250 m west of B, so +250 m for Ravi
(d) Both correct: numbers depend on the reference point and positive direction chosen

questions.q: What is the SI unit of displacement?
questions.a: The metre (m), the same SI unit as for distance travelled.

questions.q: A boy walks along a straight corridor: 30 m east, then 50 m west, then 5 m east. What are his total distance travelled and his displacement?
questions.a: Distance = 30 + 50 + 5 = 85 m; net change in position = +30 - 50 + 5 = -15 m, that is, 15 m west.

questions.q: Match each term in Column I with its meaning in Column II. Column I: 1. Distance travelled; 2. Displacement; 3. Magnitude; 4. Reference point. Column II: (a) net change in position between two instants, with direction; (b) total length of the path covered; (c) the numerical value, with units, of a quantity; (d) the fixed point from which position is measured.
questions.a: 1-b, 2-a, 3-c, 4-d: distance travelled is the total path length, displacement is the net change in position with direction, magnitude is the numerical value with units, and the reference point is the fixed point used to describe position.

questions.q: True or False: 'A ball that rolls down a straight inclined track without turning back has a total distance travelled equal to the magnitude of its displacement.' Give the verdict and the reason.
questions.a: True. In straight-line motion the distance travelled and the magnitude of displacement are equal when the object moves in one direction without turning back.
s: Reason: it moves in one direction along a straight line without turning back

questions.q: A flag on a straight vertical pole is raised 8 m and then lowered 3 m. (a) Find the total distance travelled by the flag. (b) Find its displacement.
questions.a: (a) Distance = 8 m + 3 m = 11 m. (b) Displacement = 8 m - 3 m = 5 m upward.

questions.q: Assertion (A): An object can have a displacement of zero even when the distance it has travelled is not zero. Reason (R): The magnitude of displacement is the distance between the object's positions at the two instants, whatever path it took in between.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A: if the object returns to its starting position, the distance between the two positions is zero, though it has covered a path.

questions.q: A security guard patrols a straight 60 m wall, starting at the gate G (east positive). He walks from G to the east end E, back to the middle point M (30 m from G), and then again to E. (i) Find the total distance he travels. (ii) Find his displacement from G. (iii) During which part of the walk is the distance travelled so far equal to the magnitude of his displacement?
questions.a: (i) 60 m + 30 m + 30 m = 120 m. (ii) He ends at E, 60 m east of G, so the displacement is 60 m east. (iii) Only during the first part, from G to E, because he has not yet turned back.
s: (iii) Only from G to E, before he turns back

questions.q: A squirrel moves up and down a straight vertical pole. Its height above the ground (up positive) is 4 m at the start. It climbs to 7 m, slides down to 1 m, and then climbs to 3 m, where it stops. (a) Find the total distance travelled. (b) Find its displacement from the start. (c) Give the distance travelled since the start and the magnitude of displacement at the end of each of the three moves. (d) At the end of which move are these two values equal, and why? (e) If the squirrel's starting point were taken as the reference point instead of the ground, which of your answers to (a) and (b) would change?
questions.a: (a) 3 m + 6 m + 2 m = 11 m. (b) 3 m - 4 m = -1 m, that is, 1 m downward. (c) After move 1: 3 m and 3 m; after move 2: 9 m and 3 m (downward); after move 3: 11 m and 1 m (downward). (d) Only at the end of move 1, because until then the squirrel had moved in one direction without turning back. (e) Neither: distance travelled and displacement depend only on the path and the start and end positions, not on where the reference point is; only the position numbers would change.
s: (c) 3 m and 3 m; 9 m and 3 m; 11 m and 1 m
(d) Equal only after move 1, before it turns back
(e) Neither changes; only position values depend on the reference point

questions.q: Kavya delivers newspapers. She walks 150 m west along a straight lane to the last house and then walks 150 m back to her starting point. (a) What total distance does she travel? (b) What is her displacement? (c) Which of these two quantities needs a direction to be described completely?
questions.a: (a) 150 m + 150 m = 300 m. (b) Zero, since she ends where she started. (c) Displacement needs both a magnitude and a direction; distance needs only a numerical value.

questions.q: The average speed of an object is equal to
o: total distance travelled divided by the time interval
displacement divided by the time interval
time interval divided by total distance travelled
change in velocity divided by the time interval
questions.a: Total distance travelled divided by the time interval during which that distance is covered.

questions.q: A cyclist covers 9 km in 30 minutes. What is her average speed?
questions.a: 18 km/h: 30 minutes is 0.5 h, and 9 km / 0.5 h = 18 km/h.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of uniform motion in a straight line?
o: A car on a straight road covering 15 m in every second
A bus on a straight road that stops at every signal
A ball rolling down a slope, covering more distance each second
A cyclist who slows down as she climbs a straight slope
questions.a: The car covering 15 m in every second: it covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, so it moves at constant speed.

questions.q: Which of these is moving with the greatest average speed?
o: A train covering 1.2 km in one minute
A bird flying 4.5 km in 5 minutes
questions.a: The cheetah at 25 m/s: the car's 72 km/h is 20 m/s, the train's 1.2 km per minute is 1200 m / 60 s = 20 m/s, and the bird's 4.5 km in 5 minutes is 4500 m / 300 s = 15 m/s.

questions.q: On sports day at a school in Bhopal, Meera runs a straight 100 m race from the start line to the finish line in 16 s. After the race she walks slowly back along the same straight track to the start line, which takes her 80 s. The teacher wants the class to work out how fast Meera ran and how her position changed. (a) What distance did Meera cover in the race? (b) Find her average speed during the race. (c) For the race and the walk back together, find her total distance travelled and her displacement. (d) Find her average velocity for the whole 96 s.
questions.a: (a) 100 m. (b) Average speed = 100 m / 16 s = 6.25 m/s. (c) Total distance = 100 m + 100 m = 200 m; displacement = 0 m, because she is back at the start line. (d) Average velocity = displacement / time interval = 0 m / 96 s = 0 m/s.

questions.q: A jogger runs 600 m north along a straight road in 200 s and then 300 m south along the same road in 100 s. Read the statements. I. Her average speed for the whole run is 3 m/s. II. Her average velocity for the whole run is 1 m/s towards the north. III. Her displacement for the whole run is 300 m towards the north. Which of these are correct?
questions.a: I, II and III. Total distance = 600 + 300 = 900 m, so average speed = 900 m / 300 s = 3 m/s; displacement = 600 m - 300 m = 300 m north, so average velocity = 300 m / 300 s = 1 m/s north. All three statements are correct.

questions.q: A lorry travels on a straight road for 2 hours. It first goes east, then turns back once and goes west. Its average speed for the 2 hours is 40 km/h and its average velocity is 10 km/h towards the east. How far did it go east, and how far west?
questions.a: Total distance = 40 km/h x 2 h = 80 km; displacement = 10 km/h x 2 h = 20 km east. If it goes x km east and y km west, x + y = 80 and x - y = 20, so x = 50 km east and y = 30 km west.
s: Total distance = 80 km from the average speed
Displacement = 20 km east from the average velocity
Solving: 50 km east and 30 km west

questions.q: Stations A, B and C lie in that order on a straight railway line, with AB = 60 km and BC = 90 km. A train leaves A, reaches B in 50 minutes, halts there for 10 minutes, and reaches C 60 minutes after leaving B. It then returns from C to B in 60 minutes. (a) Find the average speed from A to C, including the halt. (b) Find the average speed from A to B. (c) Is the motion from A to C uniform or non-uniform? Give a reason. (d) For the whole journey A to C to B, find the average speed and the average velocity. (e) Explain why the two answers in (d) are different.
questions.a: (a) 150 km in 50 + 10 + 60 = 120 min = 2 h, so 75 km/h. (b) 60 km in 50 min = 5/6 h, so 72 km/h. (c) Non-uniform: the train does not cover equal distances in equal time intervals (for example it covers no distance during the halt). (d) Distance = 60 + 90 + 90 = 240 km in 180 min = 3 h, so average speed = 80 km/h; displacement = 60 km from A towards C, so average velocity = 60 km / 3 h = 20 km/h towards C. (e) The train turned back at C, so the distance travelled (240 km) is greater than the magnitude of displacement (60 km).
s: (c) Non-uniform, with a reason such as the halt
(d) Average speed 80 km/h; average velocity 20 km/h towards C
(e) It turned back, so distance exceeds the magnitude of displacement

questions.q: Assertion (A): A toy car that covers 5 m in the first second, 5 m in the next second and 2 m in the third second is in non-uniform motion. Reason (R): An object in non-uniform motion always moves with decreasing speed.
o: A is true, but R is false.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.a: A is true, but R is false: the car covers unequal distances in equal time intervals, so its motion is non-uniform; but non-uniform motion can have increasing speed, decreasing speed or a combination of both.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of average acceleration?
questions.a: m/s^2 (m s-2): change in velocity (m/s) divided by time interval (s).

questions.q: A motorbike moving at 54 km/h on a straight road is braked to rest in 3 s. Taking its direction of motion as positive, what is its average acceleration?
questions.a: -5 m/s^2: 54 km/h = 15 m/s, so a = (0 - 15 m/s) / 3 s = -5 m/s^2; the minus sign shows it acts opposite to the velocity.

questions.q: A car is slowing down on a straight road. In which direction is its average acceleration?
o: Opposite to the direction of its velocity
In the same direction as its velocity
There is no acceleration while it slows down
At right angles to its velocity
questions.a: Opposite to the direction of its velocity, because the magnitude of its velocity is decreasing.

questions.q: True or False: 'A runner going round a curved part of a track at a steady 5 m/s has no average acceleration, because her speed does not change.' Give the verdict and the reason.
questions.a: False. Velocity has both magnitude and direction; on the curve the direction of her velocity keeps changing, so her velocity changes and she has an average acceleration even though her speed stays 5 m/s.
s: Reason: the direction of velocity changes on the curve, so velocity changes and there is acceleration

questions.q: A train on a straight track speeds up from 6 m/s to 22 m/s in 8 s. (a) Find its average acceleration. (b) State its direction compared with the train's velocity.
questions.a: (a) a = (22 m/s - 6 m/s) / 8 s = 16/8 = 2 m/s^2. (b) In the same direction as the velocity, because the speed is increasing.
s: (b) Same direction as the velocity, since speed increases

questions.q: A cricket ball comes straight at a fielder at 108 km/h, and the fielder stops it in 0.15 s. Taking the ball's direction of motion as positive, (i) convert its speed to m/s, (ii) find its average acceleration while being stopped, and (iii) explain what the sign of your answer tells you.
questions.a: (i) 108 km/h = 108 x 1000 m / 3600 s = 30 m/s. (ii) a = (0 - 30 m/s) / 0.15 s = -200 m/s^2. (iii) The minus sign shows the acceleration acts opposite to the ball's velocity, because the ball's speed is decreasing.
s: (iii) Minus: acceleration opposite to velocity as the ball slows

questions.q: Match each physical quantity in Column I with its SI unit in Column II. Column I: 1. Displacement; 2. Average velocity; 3. Average acceleration; 4. Time interval. Column II: (a) s; (b) m/s^2; (c) m; (d) m/s.
questions.a: 1-c, 2-d, 3-b, 4-a: displacement in metres, average velocity in metres per second, average acceleration in metres per second squared, and time interval in seconds.

questions.q: A group of students in Pune looked up how long three cars take to go from 0 km/h to 100 km/h along a straight road. Car P takes 10 s, Car Q takes 12.5 s and Car R takes 8 s. They want the magnitude of the average acceleration of each car, in m/s^2. (a) Convert 100 km/h to m/s, correct to two decimal places. (b) Find the magnitude of the average acceleration of each car. (c) Which car speeds up the fastest? (d) An advertisement says, 'Car R has the greatest acceleration, so it must have the highest speed of the three.' Evaluate this claim.
questions.a: (a) 100 km/h = 100 x 1000 m / 3600 s = 27.78 m/s. (b) P: 27.78/10 = 2.78 m/s^2; Q: 27.78/12.5 = 2.22 m/s^2; R: 27.78/8 = 3.47 m/s^2. (c) Car R, which has the largest average acceleration. (d) The claim does not follow: acceleration tells how quickly the velocity changes, not how fast the car is moving; all three reach the same 100 km/h, R only gets there sooner, and the data say nothing about the highest speed of any car.
s: (d) Claim wrong: acceleration is how quickly velocity changes, not how fast; all reach 100 km/h

questions.q: Assertion (A): A scooter moving at 5 m/s can have a larger acceleration than a car moving at 30 m/s. Reason (R): Acceleration depends not on how fast an object is moving but on how quickly its velocity is changing.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A: if the scooter's velocity is changing quickly while the car moves at a steady 30 m/s, the scooter has the larger acceleration, since the car's is zero.

questions.q: On a velocity-time graph, what does the area enclosed between the line and the time axis, for a time interval, give?
o: The displacement in that time interval
The acceleration in that time interval
The velocity at the end of the interval
The length of the time interval
questions.a: The displacement of the object in that time interval.

questions.q: What does the slope of a straight-line position-time graph give?
questions.a: The velocity: the slope is the change in position divided by the change in time, which is the average velocity.

questions.q: When the position-time graph of a vehicle is plotted, time is shown along
o: neither axis; it is written beside each point
questions.a: The X-axis (horizontal axis); position is shown along the Y-axis.

questions.q: The velocity-time graph of a cyclist is a straight line that starts from rest at 0 s and reaches 6 m/s at 8 s. What is her displacement in these 8 s?
questions.a: 24 m: the area between the line and the time axis is a triangle, 1/2 x 8 s x 6 m/s = 24 m.

questions.q: (a) What does a straight-line position-time graph tell you about the velocity of an object? (b) What does a curved position-time graph tell you?
questions.a: (a) The object is moving with a constant velocity. (b) The velocity is not constant, so the object is in accelerated (non-uniform) motion.

questions.q: The velocity-time graph of a car is a straight line from 0 m/s at 0 s to 16 m/s at 8 s. (a) Find its acceleration from the slope. (b) Find its displacement in 8 s from the area under the graph.
questions.a: (a) Slope = (16 m/s - 0 m/s) / 8 s = 2 m/s^2. (b) Area of the triangle = 1/2 x 8 s x 16 m/s = 64 m.

questions.q: On one position-time graph, the line for object A is straight from (0 s, 0 m) to (10 s, 50 m), and the line for object B is straight from (0 s, 20 m) to (10 s, 50 m). (i) Find the velocity of each. (ii) Whose line is steeper? (iii) Both lines meet at 10 s. Does this mean A and B have the same velocity at 10 s? Explain.
questions.a: (i) A: 50 m / 10 s = 5 m/s; B: (50 - 20) m / 10 s = 3 m/s. (ii) A's line is steeper, as its velocity is larger. (iii) No: meeting at 10 s only means both are at the same position (50 m) at that instant; their slopes, and so their velocities, are still 5 m/s and 3 m/s.
s: (iii) No: same position, not same slope or velocity

questions.q: A scooter moves in a straight line. Its velocity-time graph is a straight line from 4 m/s at 0 s to 12 m/s at 8 s, followed by a straight line parallel to the time axis at 12 m/s from 8 s to 14 s. (a) Find the acceleration in the first 8 s. (b) Find the displacement in the first 8 s. (c) Find the displacement from 8 s to 14 s. (d) Find the total displacement and the average velocity for the 14 s. (e) Describe the shape of the position-time graph in each of the two parts.
questions.a: (a) Slope = (12 - 4) m/s / 8 s = 1 m/s^2. (b) Area = rectangle 4 m/s x 8 s + triangle 1/2 x 8 s x 8 m/s = 32 m + 32 m = 64 m. (c) Rectangle 12 m/s x 6 s = 72 m. (d) Total = 64 m + 72 m = 136 m; average velocity = 136 m / 14 s = 9.7 m/s (about). (e) First part: a curve, since the velocity is changing; second part: a straight sloped line, since the velocity is constant.
s: (e) Curve, then a straight sloped line

questions.q: A farm in Nashik tests a spraying drone that flies in a straight line along a row of crops. Its controller records the drone's velocity every 2 s after take-off along the row: 0 m/s at 0 s, 3 m/s at 2 s, 6 m/s at 4 s, 9 m/s at 6 s and 12 m/s at 8 s. The farmer plots these values as a velocity-time graph. (a) Is the acceleration constant? Give a reason from the data. (b) Find the acceleration from the slope of the graph. (c) Find the displacement in the 8 s from the area under the graph. (d) Compare the displacement in the first 4 s with that in the next 4 s.
questions.a: (a) Yes: the velocity rises by the same 3 m/s in every 2 s, so the graph is a straight line and the acceleration is constant. (b) Slope = (12 - 0) m/s / 8 s = 1.5 m/s^2. (c) Area of the triangle = 1/2 x 8 s x 12 m/s = 48 m. (d) First 4 s: 1/2 x 4 s x 6 m/s = 12 m; next 4 s: 48 m - 12 m = 36 m, which is three times as much, because the drone moves faster later.
s: (a) Constant: equal rise of 3 m/s in every 2 s
(d) 12 m then 36 m: three times more in the later 4 s

questions.q: Which of these is one of the kinematic equations for motion in a straight line with constant acceleration?
questions.a: v = u + at, which gives the velocity at time t from the initial velocity and the constant acceleration.

questions.q: A trolley starts from rest and moves in a straight line with a constant acceleration of 2 m/s^2. What is its velocity after 6 s?

Assertion (A): The equation v^2 = u^2 + 2as can give the stopping distance of a vehicle even when the time it takes to stop is not known. Reason (R): The equation v^2 = u^2 + 2as is obtained by eliminating the acceleration a from the other two kinematic equations.
o: A is true, but R is false.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.a: A is true, but R is false: v^2 = u^2 + 2as does not contain t, so the stopping distance can be found without the time; it is obtained by eliminating the time t, not the acceleration.

questions.q: A bus starts from rest and moves along a straight road with a constant acceleration of 1 m/s^2. (a) Find its velocity after 10 s. (b) Find the distance it covers in these 10 s.
s: (a) v = 10 m/s using v = u + at
(b) s = 50 m using s = ut + 1/2 at^2

questions.q: True or False: 'A cart that starts from rest and moves with a constant acceleration covers more distance in the second 2 s of its motion than in the first 2 s.' Give the verdict and the reason.
questions.a: True. With a = 2 m/s^2, for example, s = 1/2 at^2 gives 4 m in the first 2 s and 16 m in 4 s, so 12 m in the second 2 s; its velocity keeps increasing, so it covers more distance in each later interval.
s: Reason: velocity keeps rising; s = 1/2 at^2 gives a larger distance in the later 2 s

questions.q: A motorbike moving at 20 m/s on a straight road brakes with a constant acceleration and stops in 5 s. (i) Find its acceleration. (ii) Find the distance it travels while stopping, using s = ut + 1/2 at^2. (iii) Check your answer to (ii) using v^2 = u^2 + 2as.

A train enters a station at 30 m/s and must stop, with a constant acceleration, before the end of the platform, which is 150 m ahead. The engineer can choose one of two brake settings: -2.5 m/s^2 or -3.5 m/s^2. (a) Find the smallest magnitude of acceleration that would just stop the train in 150 m. (b) Find the stopping distance with the -2.5 m/s^2 setting. (c) Find the stopping distance with the -3.5 m/s^2 setting. (d) Which setting should the engineer choose? Justify your decision.
questions.a: (a) 0 = 30^2 + 2a x 150 gives a = -900/300 = -3 m/s^2, so a magnitude of 3 m/s^2. (b) s = 30^2 / (2 x 2.5) = 900/5 = 180 m. (c) s = 900 / (2 x 3.5) = 900/7 = 128.6 m (about). (d) The -3.5 m/s^2 setting: it stops the train in about 128.6 m, within the 150 m, while -2.5 m/s^2 needs 180 m and the train would overshoot the platform by 30 m.
s: (d) Choose -3.5 m/s^2: stops within 150 m; -2.5 m/s^2 overshoots by 30 m

questions.q: A ball starts from rest and rolls down a straight slope with a constant acceleration of 2 m/s^2 for 5 s. (a) Write the kinematic equation that gives the velocity at time t. (b) Find the velocity of the ball at 5 s. (c) Find the distance it rolls in 5 s. (d) Check your answers to (b) and (c) using v^2 = u^2 + 2as. (e) Find the distance it rolls in the first 1 s.

A car in Bengaluru joins a highway from a straight slip road that is 150 m long. It enters the slip road at 10 m/s and must reach the highway traffic speed of 25 m/s before the slip road ends. With a constant acceleration of 2 m/s^2 the car speeds up smoothly. Another driver says, 'Even with a gentler acceleration of 1.5 m/s^2, I will reach 25 m/s before the slip road ends.' (a) Using v = u + at, find the time the car takes to reach 25 m/s at 2 m/s^2. (b) Using s = ut + 1/2 at^2, find the distance it covers in that time. (c) Find the time and the distance needed at 1.5 m/s^2. (d) Evaluate the other driver's claim.
questions.a: (a) t = (v - u) / a = (25 - 10) / 2 = 7.5 s. (b) s = 10 x 7.5 + 1/2 x 2 x 7.5^2 = 75 + 56.25 = 131.25 m, which is within the 150 m. (c) t = (25 - 10) / 1.5 = 10 s; s = 10 x 10 + 1/2 x 1.5 x 10^2 = 100 + 75 = 175 m. (d) The claim is wrong: at 1.5 m/s^2 the car needs 175 m, which is 25 m more than the 150 m slip road, so it would reach the end still below 25 m/s.
s: (d) Claim wrong: 175 m needed but only 150 m available

questions.q: An object goes once round a circular path of radius R. What distance does it travel?
questions.a: 2 pi R, the circumference of the circle (its displacement after the full revolution is zero).

questions.q: Which of these is an example of motion in a plane (motion in two dimensions)?
o: The path of a football kicked into the air
A ball dropped straight down from a balcony
A train moving on a straight track
A lift moving straight up its shaft
questions.a: The path of a kicked football, which curves through a plane; the other three are motions in a straight line.

questions.q: True or False: 'In uniform circular motion, the velocity of the object at any point is directed towards the centre of the circle.' Give the verdict and the reason.
questions.a: False. The velocity at any point is along the tangent to the circle at that point, in the direction of motion.
s: Reason: velocity is along the tangent at that point, in the direction of motion

questions.q: A toy train runs round a circular track of radius 0.7 m at a constant speed and takes 11 s for one round. Taking pi = 22/7, (a) find the distance travelled in one round, and (b) find its average speed.
questions.a: (a) 2 pi R = 2 x 22/7 x 0.7 m = 4.4 m. (b) Average speed = 4.4 m / 11 s = 0.4 m/s.

questions.q: An athlete runs round a circular track at a steady speed. Read the statements. I. Because her speed does not change, her motion is not accelerated. II. At each point, her velocity is along the tangent to the circle at that point. III. The direction of her velocity changes continuously. Which of these are correct?
questions.a: II and III only. Her velocity at each point is along the tangent, and its direction changes continuously, so her velocity changes and her motion is accelerated even at a steady speed. Statement I is wrong.

questions.q: A car goes round a circular test track of radius 70 m at a constant speed of 11 m/s. Taking pi = 22/7, (i) find the time for one lap, (ii) find its displacement after half a lap, and (iii) compare its average velocity over half a lap with its average speed.
questions.a: (i) T = 2 pi R / speed = (2 x 22/7 x 70 m) / 11 m/s = 440/11 = 40 s. (ii) After half a lap it is at the opposite end of a diameter, so the displacement is 2R = 140 m. (iii) Half a lap takes 20 s, so the average velocity has magnitude 140 m / 20 s = 7 m/s, less than the average speed of 11 m/s, because the straight-line displacement is shorter than the curved path.
s: (iii) 7 m/s average velocity, less than 11 m/s speed, with reason

questions.q: A toy train runs at a constant speed on a circular track of radius 3.5 m laid on the floor. It makes 3 full revolutions in 66 s. Taking pi = 22/7, (a) find the distance travelled in one revolution. (b) Find the total distance travelled and the average speed for the 66 s. (c) Find the displacement and the average velocity for the 66 s. (d) Find the magnitude of the average velocity for the first half revolution. (e) The train's speed never changes. Explain why its motion is still accelerated.
questions.a: (a) 2 pi R = 2 x 22/7 x 3.5 m = 22 m. (b) 3 x 22 m = 66 m, so the average speed = 66 m / 66 s = 1 m/s. (c) The train is back at the start after 3 full revolutions, so the displacement is 0 m and the average velocity is 0 m/s. (d) One revolution takes 22 s, so half takes 11 s; the displacement is one diameter, 7 m, so the average velocity is 7 m / 11 s = 0.64 m/s (about). (e) The direction of the train's velocity, along the tangent, changes continuously, and a change in the direction of velocity is a change in velocity, so there is acceleration.
s: (e) Direction of velocity changes continuously, so velocity changes
